assumptions: The locomotive makes a steady level turn. Consider only the turbine’s gyroscopic contribution, apart from static weight and centrifugal load transfer.
Define x forward, y left, z up. Forward-rolling wheels and the turbine have spin angular momentum +Hy. A left turn has precession +Ωz.

steps.explanation: Convert the turbine speed and locomotive speed, then find the yaw rate.
The required torque on the turbine is backward along the locomotive, and its reaction on the vehicle is forward.
steps.math_latex: \boldsymbol\tau_{\rm bearings\to turbine}=\Omega\mathbf z\times H\mathbf y=-\Omega H\mathbf x,\qquad \mathbf N_{\rm turbine\to vehicle}=+\Omega H\mathbf x.

steps.explanation: Equal and opposite additional vertical rail forces separated by the gauge l transmit this couple. Their magnitude is moment divided by gauge.
For a left turn the outer right rail acquires extra downward force and the inner left rail is unloaded. Their net vertical increment is zero but their moment is +N x on the rails.
steps.math_latex: \Delta\mathbf F_{\rm outer}=-\Delta F\,\mathbf z,\qquad \Delta\mathbf F_{\rm inner}=+\Delta F\,\mathbf z.
